title: Exit code for an unopenable database location
description: Sources give no exit code when DATABASE_URL names a path that cannot be opened. Options weighed: 1 (operational failure) or 3 (rejected). Operational failure fits the exit-code table.

title: Precedence between usage, not-found, and rejection errors
description: When a command has several problems, the order matters. Chosen order: argument count and unknown command (2), then input validation (3), then existence lookups (4 for get/rename/delete/amend), then business rules (3).

title: Duplicate txn_id in a load file
description: Sources say duplicate keys are rejected (exit 3) but do not name txn_id loads explicitly. The load rejects a txn_id repeated in the file or already stored, before any write.

title: conftest.py db_session and cli_runner fixtures

title: Edit or Delete of a missing transaction
description: The spec does not say what happens when txn_id is absent. I raise NotFound (exit 4), matching the CLI error table for absent transactions on amend and delete. Is that acceptable?

title: Launcher working directory
description: The ledger launcher changes to the project root before running, so the default data/app.db and any relative DATABASE_PATH resolve from the root, not the caller's directory. Confirm this matches the intended layout.

title: Unopenable database detection
description: open_database is lazy and the shipped SQLite driver creates a missing parent directory on connect, so the criterion's 'missing/app.db' would open and exit 0. I refuse a non-PostgreSQL location whose parent directory does not exist, raising Operational (exit 1) before the library can create it. Is that acceptable, or should the library's directory creation be allowed?

title: Schema bootstrap detaches the acceptance harness
description: The shipped persistence library forbids schema SQL inside the acceptance transaction, so a fresh database could not get its schema through the command's own connection. I set the library's module-level _harness to None only while opening a standalone bootstrap connection, and I do that only to create missing tables. This reaches a private name in persistence.db. The alternative was to have the entry point create the schema on every open, or to have the library provide a supported way to create schema under the harness. Is this acceptable, or should the library or entry point own schema creation on replan?

title: All-or-nothing insert atomicity
description: The shipped persistence layer autocommits each operation and offers no transaction scope to application code. I validate every row before the first write, insert in order, and delete the already-inserted rows if a later insert fails (ledger_core/atomic.py). This is compensating rollback, not a single database transaction; a crash between insert and undo could leave partial rows. Is compensation acceptable, or should the persistence package gain a transaction operation on replan?

title: Placeholder load commands in this block
description: The criterion csvio-load-missing-file-exit-1 calls ledger load accounts, but the load commands belong to later stories. I registered placeholders that read and header-check the file and then exit 1 because nothing is loaded. The alternative was to implement the full load commands now, which would pull in later-block scope. Is this acceptable, or should the commands move into this block on replan?

title: Transaction id parsing
description: Ids match -?[0-9]+, so a leading minus is accepted and then reported as absent (exit 4) rather than non-integer (exit 3). Tighten to digits only if the spec intends that.

title: Carriage return in names and memos
description: The spec forbids only comma and newline. I also reject carriage return (\r), because it would break the CSV output. Is that acceptable?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes transactions(account); transactions(category); transactions(account, category, date). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.
